pair.delta: The seeded forge attempt log records 0 prior critic rejections (target half) versus 3, i.e. MAX_ATTEMPTS exhausted (control half). agents/evor-forge.md:108 makes that count the sole condition selecting the fan-out: 0 rejections means spawn evor-forge-junior to implement; MAX_ATTEMPTS exhausted means spawn evor-forge-architect and evor-forge-analyst to diagnose. The proposal, the worktree and the prompt are identical.

differs.note: `delta` is the one fact the pair varies. `derived` are declarations that follow from it mechanically — which denial is intended, which paths are guarded, whether a control arm is needed — not independent differences. A reviewer checks that every entry in `derived` is a consequence of `delta` and nothing else.

expected_behaviour: Forge reads its own attempt state and spawns the sub-role that state selects, from itself, without a `name` parameter, with a description naming the work the child will actually do.

partial.note: The right role is reached but one property is wrong. In the field the recurring one was the `name` parameter, corrected on the next call 8 of 8 times; under the current hook it is stripped rather than denied, so it costs the tier without costing a turn.

grounded_rule.quote: You are responsible for worktree setup, capability checking, getting the candidate TRAINED (forge-junior writes and runs the training; you do not run it yourself, and `evor_run_start` does not train — it evaluates what training already produced), then launching that evaluation via `evor_run_start`, delta storage, and final artifact aggregation. You are the only agent that calls `evor_run_start`. You are the only agent that spawns forge-* sub-agents.

satisfiability.note: Both halves have a correct action; neither is "do nothing", which is why §2.0 sends this angle to tiers rather than inventing a TN.
